transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've got a cough, and I've been getting a pain on the right side of my abdomen. It started two days ago.
Could you describe how bad the cough and the pain are and how they’re affecting you day to day, and also let me know if you have any allergies or have had bad reactions to medicines?
The cough is a dry one, and the pain in my abdomen only comes on when I cough. I haven't noticed any allergies or bad reactions to medicines.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have taken recently, and any health problems, operations, or hospital stays you’ve had in the past?

I have high blood pressure and macular degeneration, and I had pneumonia last year that cleared up. I've not had any operations that I can remember, and I'm sorry but I can't remember the names of any medicines I take.
How bad would you say the cough and the pain are on a scale of 0 to 10, and how much are they affecting your day-to-day activities?

I'm sorry, I can't really put a number on them — I haven't thought of it that way. The pain only comes when I cough, so it's not there the rest of the time, but I have been feeling generally achy and a bit nauseous, and I've felt feverish with chills at home.
Since this started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder, bowel habits, or breathing? If not, that’s completely fine.

I haven't really noticed any changes in my appetite, sleep, weight or energy, and nothing different with my bladder or bowels. My breathing seems fine apart from the cough — the only other thing has been the nausea I mentioned.

Could you describe in your own words how the cough and the pain on the right side of your tummy come and go — whether they’re there all the time or on and off, how often they happen, how long each episode lasts, and whether any time of day makes a difference?

The pain isn't there all the time — it only comes on when I cough, and it goes once the coughing stops. Beyond that I can't really say how often it happens or whether any time of day makes a difference; it's just been since it started two days ago.

Besides the high blood pressure, macular degeneration and the pneumonia last year, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly, or any other operations or hospital stays you can think of? If not, that’s completely fine.
No, I don't think so — the blood pressure and macular degeneration are the main things I see them about, and I can't think of any other operations or hospital stays.
What worries you most about what’s been going on, and what are you hoping we can help with today?
I'm most concerned that the cough and this pain in my side haven't settled after two days, and I'd like to know what's causing them. I'm hoping you can help me feel better.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
